questions.prompt: Determine whether \(S=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x-2y+z=0\}\) is closed under addition.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(x_i-2y_i+z_i=0\) for \(i=1,2\), then
\[(x_1+x_2)-2(y_1+y_2)+(z_1+z_2)=0+0=0.\]
Final answer: \(S\) is closed under addition.

questions.prompt: Determine whether the polynomials of degree exactly \(2\), together with the usual operations, form a vector space.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Both \(p(x)=x^2\) and \(q(x)=-x^2\) have degree \(2\), but
\[p+q=0,\]
which does not have degree exactly \(2\).
Final answer: The set is not a vector space.

questions.prompt: Test closure under addition for \(S=\{A\in M_{2}(\mathbb R):\operatorname{tr}A=0\}\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For \(A,B\in S\), linearity of trace gives
\[\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}A+\operatorname{tr}B=0.\]
Final answer: \(S\) is closed under addition.

questions.prompt: Determine the additive inverse of \((x,y)\) under \((x,y)\oplus(u,v)=(x+u-1,y+v-2)\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
First find the additive identity \(\mathbf0_\oplus\):
\[(x,y)\oplus(a,b)=(x,y)\Rightarrow(a,b)=(1,2).\]
For the inverse \((u,v)\), solve
\[(x+u-1,y+v-2)=(1,2),\]
so \(u=2-x\), \(v=4-y\).
Final answer: The additive inverse is \((2-x,4-y)\).

questions.prompt: Verify associativity of \(\oplus\) defined by \(x\oplus y=x+y+1\) on \(\mathbb R\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
\[(x\oplus y)\oplus z=(x+y+1)+z+1=x+y+z+2,\]
\[x\oplus(y\oplus z)=x+(y+z+1)+1=x+y+z+2.\]
Final answer: \((x\oplus y)\oplus z=x\oplus(y\oplus z)\).

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(S=\{f\in C^1(\mathbb R):f(0)=0\}\) is closed under \(af+bg\) for arbitrary real \(a,b\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For \(f,g\in S\),
\[(af+bg)(0)=af(0)+bg(0)=0.\]
Final answer: \(af+bg\in S\), so \(S\) is closed under linear combinations.

questions.prompt: Test whether \(S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:xy=0\}\) is closed under addition.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
The vectors \((1,0),(0,1)\in S\), but
\[(1,0)+(0,1)=(1,1),\qquad1\cdot1\ne0.\]
Final answer: \(S\) is not closed under addition.

questions.prompt: Determine whether the symmetric \(3\times3\) real matrices form a vector space.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For symmetric \(A,B\) and real \(c\),
\[(A+B)^{\mathsf T}=A^{\mathsf T}+B^{\mathsf T}=A+B,\qquad(cA)^{\mathsf T}=cA^{\mathsf T}=cA.\]
The zero matrix is symmetric, and additive inverses remain symmetric.
Final answer: The symmetric \(3\times3\) matrices form a vector space.

questions.prompt: Determine whether \(S=\{p\in P_3:p(1)=p'(1)=0\}\) is a vector space.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For \(p,q\in S\) and scalars \(a,b\),
\[(ap+bq)(1)=0,\qquad(ap+bq)'(1)=ap'(1)+bq'(1)=0.\]
Also the zero polynomial satisfies both conditions.
Final answer: \(S\) is a vector space.

questions.prompt: Test all scalar distributive axioms for \(a\odot(x,y)=(ax,0)\) with ordinary addition on \(\mathbb R^2\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Although \(a\odot(\mathbf u+\mathbf v)=a\odot\mathbf u+a\odot\mathbf v\) and \((a+b)\odot\mathbf u=a\odot\mathbf u+b\odot\mathbf u\), the unit axiom fails:
\[1\odot(x,y)=(x,0)\ne(x,y)\]
when \(y\ne0\).
Final answer: The operation fails the scalar identity axiom and does not define a vector space.

questions.prompt: Determine all real \(c\) for which \(S_c=\{(x,y):x+y=c\}\) is a vector space under ordinary operations.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
A vector space must contain \((0,0)\), requiring \(0+0=c\), so \(c=0\). For \(c=0\), the equation is homogeneous and is preserved by linear combinations.
Final answer: \(S_c\) is a vector space exactly when \(c=0\).

questions.prompt: Construct a counterexample to closure under addition for the invertible \(2\times2\) real matrices.

Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Choose two invertible matrices
\[A=I,\qquad B=-I.\]
Both have nonzero determinant, but
\[A+B=0\]
is singular.
Final answer: \(I\) and \(-I\) are an explicit counterexample.

questions.prompt: Determine all real \(k\) for which \(S_k=\{(x,y,z):x+ky+z=0\}\) is a vector space.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
For every real \(k\), the defining equation is homogeneous. If \(L_k(x,y,z)=x+ky+z\), then
\[L_k(a\mathbf u+b\mathbf v)=aL_k(\mathbf u)+bL_k(\mathbf v)=0.\]
Final answer: Every \(k\in\mathbb R\) gives a vector space.

questions.prompt: Prove that the intersection \(U\cap W\) of two subspaces of a vector space \(V\) is a subspace.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Since \(\mathbf0\in U\) and \(\mathbf0\in W\), \(\mathbf0\in U\cap W\). If \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v\in U\cap W\) and \(a,b\) are scalars, then \(a\mathbf u+b\mathbf v\in U\) and \(a\mathbf u+b\mathbf v\in W\). Hence it belongs to the intersection.
Final answer: \(U\cap W\) is a subspace of \(V\).

questions.prompt: Prove that \(S=\{\mathbf x\in V:T\mathbf x=\mathbf0\}\) is a vector space when \(T:V\to W\) is linear.
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
Linearity gives \(T\mathbf0=\mathbf0\), so \(\mathbf0\in S\). For \(\mathbf x,\mathbf y\in S\),
\[T(a\mathbf x+b\mathbf y)=aT\mathbf x+bT\mathbf y=\mathbf0.\]
Final answer: \(S=\ker T\) is a vector space.

questions.prompt: Prove that the union of two subspaces \(U\cup W\) is a subspace if and only if \(U\subseteq W\) or \(W\subseteq U\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If one subspace contains the other, the union equals the larger subspace. Conversely, suppose neither inclusion holds. Choose \(\mathbf u\in U\setminus W\) and \(\mathbf w\in W\setminus U\). If \(\mathbf u+\mathbf w\in U\), then \(\mathbf w=(\mathbf u+\mathbf w)-\mathbf u\in U\), a contradiction. If it lies in \(W\), then \(\mathbf u\in W\), also a contradiction. Thus the union is not closed under addition.
Final answer: \(U\cup W\) is a subspace exactly when one subspace contains the other.

questions.prompt: Prove that the solution set of \(A\mathbf x=\mathbf b\) is a vector space exactly when it is nonempty and \(\mathbf b=\mathbf0\), apart from the degenerate case \(A=0\).
questions.answer:
We need to complete the stated vector-space calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the relevant vector-space definitions and solve the resulting equations.
If \(\mathbf b=\mathbf0\), the solution set is \(\ker A\), hence a vector space. Conversely, a vector-space solution set contains \(\mathbf0\), so
\[A\mathbf0=\mathbf0=\mathbf b.\]
Thus \(\mathbf b=\mathbf0\). If \(A=0\) and \(\mathbf b\ne0\), the set is empty and is not a vector space.
Final answer: A nonempty solution set is a vector space if and only if \(\mathbf b=\mathbf0\).
